theory.intro: The **vertical line test** decides whether a graph is a function. Sweep a vertical line across it: if every position meets it at most once, it is a function. If any position meets it more than once, it is not.
facts: A vertical line marks one $x$-value, so meeting the graph twice means that $x$ has two different $y$-values.
A closed circle $\bullet$ means the point is on the graph; an open circle $\circ$ means it is not.
An open point does not count as a crossing.
Circles, sideways (left- or right-opening) parabolas and vertical lines fail; non-vertical straight lines, upright parabolas, upper and lower semicircles, cubics and exponentials pass.

workedExamples.question_text: Give an example of a straight line that is not a function. Explain why it fails the vertical line test.

foundation.solution_text:
Every vertical line meets the straight line at exactly one point.
Yes, it is a function.

Any vertical line meets this upright parabola at just one point.
Yes, it is a function.

A vertical line through the middle of the circle cuts it at two points (a top and a bottom).
No, it is not a function.

The graph is itself a vertical line, so a vertical line at $x = 1$ lies along it and meets it at infinitely many points.
No, it is not a function.

This is only the top half of a circle, so any vertical line meets it at most once.
Yes, it is a function.

This sideways parabola opens to the left, so a vertical line cuts it at two points.
No, it is not a function.

Every vertical line meets this exponential curve exactly once.
Yes, it is a function.

development.solution_text:
Although the curve turns, any single vertical line still meets it at just one point.
Yes, it is a function.

Every vertical line meets the graph at most once, with no intersection at $x = 0$.
Yes, it is a function.

At $x = 1$ the graph has a filled point at $(1, -1)$ and an open point at $(1, 2)$; the open point is not on the graph.
Every vertical line meets the graph at most once.
Yes, it is a function.

This parabola opens downwards, but any vertical line still meets it just once.
Yes, it is a function.

mastery.solution_text:
A vertical line, such as $x = -1.5$, is a straight line.
A vertical test line placed at that same $x$ lies along the whole line, meeting it at infinitely many points.
So a vertical line fails the test and is not a function.

At $x = 2$ the open point $(2, 1)$ is **not** on the graph, so it does not count as a crossing.
Only the filled point $(2, 3)$ lies on the graph there, so the vertical line $x = 2$ meets it once.
Yes, it is a function.

The vertical line $x = 0.5$ cuts the circle twice.
Those points are $(0.5, 1.5)$ and $(0.5, -1.5)$, which share the same $x$-value.

practice.coverageNote: A yes/no categorical skill applied to coordinate graphs; variety comes from the range of graph shapes (line, parabola, circle, semicircle, sideways parabola, cubic, hyperbola, exponential, vertical line, piecewise) plus the "give two points" case for non-functions.
